wanted to make sure that the name aliases worked.  Easiest way to do that is to build two different commits, one that does the rename, and one that applies it everywhere

does `clang-rename` help here? I've only really used it for C symbols, so not sure how it copes with namespace renames.

Here's how I use it in practice:

1. A wrapper script to drive it: https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/scripts/apply-renames
2. A bunch of rename configs: https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/tree/main/evolutions/v0.9.1

I haven't used clang-rename, but that would seem like it would attempt to fix other peoples code.  All of bmcweb itself can be migrated in one shot with just sed, it's a matter of peoples patchsets being able to rebase, which this at least makes their existing code continue to work.

Overall I support this. 

Some additional sentences here or before.. 
"bmcweb was originally based on Crow. Crow is a C++ framework for creating HTTP or Websocket web services. The crow functionality has been replaced by boost beast, etc."
